Hello fellow wow players! I figured since there's not too much here I might actually try and contribute something to help get people talking. So, like the title says, what's your favorite memory of wow?

I'd have to say my favorite was the time that a bunch of my IRL and in-game friends went "under Stormwind" way back when, and just messed around. Made our own little area, and just did a whole lot of nothing. Kind of funny, when you consider that it really had nothing to do with the game itself, but it was just a fun bonding experience, and the friendship beats any achievements in my mind.

Oh man, yes! I remember trying to get in all sorts of those "secret" places back in the day. I'd spend so much time finding YouTube videos and then jumping and jumping and jumping.... I particularly remember getting into caverns of time before it was released and then waiting for friends to get online to show them!

Oh I remember this so well.

There used to be a glitch in one of the walls in the Trade District, where you could manage to jump up on top and fall through under the city. It was awesome because it was this huge blank space where you could just run for ages. You could take your mount up through Elwynn into Dun Morogh, and manage to hitchhike up over the mountains a certain way. Fun memories.

For me, the best glitch was getting trying to get into Vanilla Hyjal, which was pretty awesome because it was so mysterious and untouched. Apparently a long time ago, if you managed to get in through Frostwhisper Gorge, you'd get killed by some 'Guardians of Blizzard' bears. Super interesting.

Yep, it was the one in Trade that I always used. I remember trying for 30 or more minutes for us all to get under, because it was easier with a mount, but I was too poor to have one back then. Lots of fun.

And getting into Hyjal was probably the coolest place; I don't remember any bears, but I do remember that they had it blocked off and, if you managed to get through, you would just automatically die and have to resurrect back at the spirit healer.

We were in the living room at my parents house, all of us with our laptops, sitting next to each other playing WoW for the entire weekend. I'm not even sure what we were doing in WoW at the time, either puging wotlk or dungeons, but it doesn't matter to me. WoW brought us together and I really miss those moments.

It's so hard to choose a favorite. Here are a few that really stick out for me.

--My first Ragnaros kill: To me, WoW has always been a game about competition. Though I arrived to the raid scene very late (hit 60 in April 2006), I knew that the first step to feeling good about myself in-game was clearing Molten Core. There's a whole backstory of fortuitous coincidences and chance happenings that led to me getting in a decent starter guild, but it happened, and I got to see what it was like to take part in building a guild from scratch to killing Ragnaros. That first Ragnaros kill was momentous. All the months of leveling, grinding 5-mans, and spamming ZG/AQ20 a few times a week, all those hours in Arathi Highlands farming fire resist pot mats, and all the weeks of progression in Molten Core, all finally culminated in that kill. I finally felt I had arrived and I earned it. Hell, even the kill attempt has a story behind it. Great memory.

--Seeing Kel'Thuzad for the first time. After ~6 months of progression in Naxx (different guild than my MC guild) I remember killing Sapphiron and entering that curved hall that leads to KT's room. When I rounded that corner and saw KT for the first time, I remember feeling like oh my fucking god, I've worked so hard for this. I can't believe I'm finally here. I only killed him twice pre-TBC, but literally just seeing him was so gratifying. I didn't think it would happen, and it totally did.

--M'uru kill. Back in TBC, cooldowns like shield wall, lay on hands, and other similar skills could only be used once or twice per hour. I want to say shield wall was 30 minutes. So blowing those CDs was no light decision. After over 500 wipes on M'uru (still cited by some as the hardest boss in the game's history, though imo that's probably been eclipsed by one or two others), we finally had an attempt where our execution and dc rng were good enough to close in for the kill. If you did M'uru back then, you will recall the Entropius phase as being a race to the finish. It's one of those fights where just moments into it, people start dropping and it gets harder and harder per death. As we broke into the single-digit realm, it seemed like a kill was very likely. We blew all shield walls, all lay on hands, etc. Everyone was going berserk on vent. We had it. Except we didn't. It was a 1% wipe. I'd have to check screenshots but it might have been a 0% wipe. It was extremely close, but we didn't get it, and we blew everything, so in the next attempt, we would have no major cooldowns available. But at that point, we were so resolved to finish the fucking thing that we decided to have another pull. It was intense as fuck. Our execution was incredible and we got the kill. That whole experience was amazing.

Since TBC, I've really chilled on raiding, so there aren't many awesome memories. I got a few world rank 1 DPS parses in MoP early-on, which felt amazing for me, personally, but that was almost three years ago at this point. I still love the game, and I love these memories, but I'm not sure I'll have any more like them.

The sense of community that existed on US-Frostmourne back in the day. Back in vanilla and even BC, gosh. The community was still fairly close-knit, and guilds were even more close-knit. Whilst the guild I was in was run by a dragon (my husband's ex-girlfriend, haha), everyone was pretty tight.

I can remember running Mag's Lair in BC and everyone aceing the cube clicking. That shit doesn't happen now.

We've jumped from realm to realm since Frostmourne, with only my husband and I being the remnants of the original group. We have a friend still raiding with us who we originally met in WotLK, but everyone else is new from MOP.
